mainTopic: When a missing part or a blemish disqualifies a קרבן: the timing up to קבלה, hidden versus visible blemishes, and the משנה's blemishes of the זובן and tail
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא settled two conflicting ברייתות about an animal missing a kidney: one case is before שחיטה, the other after. Here, רבי זירא in the name of רב shows that a מום after שחיטה but before קבלה still disqualifies, so the גמרא moves the dividing line to קבלה. A ברייתא about the קרבן פסח seems to require the animal to be תמים all the way through זריקה. The גמרא answers that this later requirement is only about being בן שנה, and it supports this with רבי יהושע's rule that blood is sprinkled even if only a כזית remains. From this, רבא learns that age in קדשים is counted to the exact hour (שעות פוסלות). The גמרא then tries to show that whether a hidden lack counts is a dispute among תנאים about blemishes of the ביצים. It rejects that idea because of רבי יוסי's split view, and explains that they really argue about which blemishes are visible. A new משנה lists blemishes of the זובן and the tail. The גמרא limits the זובן blemish to damage rather than removal, and defines the finger measure as a quarter of a טפח, which רבה links to ציצית. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע links it instead to the two measuring cubits, a source that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blemish after slaughter but before collecting the blood disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer, which split the cases into before and after שחיטה. It cites רבי זירא in the name of רב: if someone slits the bull's ear after שחיטה and only then does קבלה, the קרבן is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי זירא say in the name of רב: if someone slits the ear of the bull and only afterward collects its blood, it is disqualified. The פסוק says "and he shall take from the blood of the bull," meaning the bull as it already was before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its earlier answer. A source shows that a מום appearing after שחיטה can still disqualify the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said a missing kidney only matters if the loss happened before שחיטה. רב says that a מום created after שחיטה, but before קבלה, still makes the קרבן פסול. The word "הפר" ("the bull") teaches that at קבלה the bull must still be the same perfect bull it was before.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slits or nicks (here, the ear), creating a מום
Collected its blood in a כלי שרת (the עבודה called קבלה)
Disqualified as a קרבן
The bull as it already was, meaning still unblemished

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that once the animal is slaughtered, any later damage no longer matters. According to רב, the animal must still be תמים at קבלה, even though שחיטה is already done.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Zeira say in the name of Rav:
One who slits the ear of the bull
and afterward collected its blood: it is disqualified,
as it is stated: "And he shall take from the blood of the bull"
meaning the bull as it already was!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier resolution (before or after שחיטה) that came on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier distinction that a missing kidney only disqualifies if it went missing before שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that a מום formed after שחיטה but before קבלה disqualifies. So the line cannot simply be שחיטה.

steps.title: The dividing line is collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises its answer. The ברייתא that disqualifies refers to an animal that lost the kidney before קבלה. The ברייתא that permits refers to an animal that lost it after קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: here it is speaking of an animal that became lacking before קבלה, and there of one that became lacking after קבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the two-case approach but moves the dividing line from שחיטה to קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רב's ruling, since a מום before קבלה disqualifies. It still explains why one ברייתא allows a missing kidney: the loss happened only after קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals a revised answer)
Here… there (splitting two sources into two cases)
That became lacking (missing a part)
Collecting the blood

phrases.english: Rather: here, where it became lacking before the collection of the blood,
there, where it became lacking after the collection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of רב by shifting the dividing point to קבלה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the cases (אוקימתא) by moving the timing line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dividing line was שחיטה: before it the animal is disqualified, after it the animal is fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dividing line is קבלה: a loss before קבלה disqualifies, a loss after קבלה does not.

steps.title: Is a loss after collection but before sprinkling really allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the new answer. A ברייתא about the קרבן פסח teaches that the animal must be תמים and בן שנה at the time of שחיטה, and it is about to extend this to later stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And after קבלה but before זריקה, is it really permitted? But it was taught in a ברייתא: "A lamb without blemish, a male in its first year, it shall be for you." This means it must be תמים and בן שנה at the time of שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer and begins quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer allows a loss between קבלה and זריקה. The ברייתא opens by requiring תמים at שחיטה, and its continuation will extend that requirement through זריקה. That would contradict the answer just given.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח
Is it permitted? (a rhetorical challenge)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
Unblemished, whole
Within its first year

phrases.english: And after the collection but before the sprinkling,
is it permitted?
But isn't it taught: "A lamb without blemish, a male in its first year
shall it be for you"
that it shall be unblemished and in its first year
at the time of slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַחַר קַבָּלָה קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה, מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new dividing line (קבלה) just proposed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a loss after קבלה but before זריקה does not disqualify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires תמים at every stage of the עבודה, including זריקה (completed in the next step).

steps.title: The ברייתא extends the requirement through sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: from the word "יהיה" we learn that the animal must be תמים and בן שנה at קבלה, הולכה, and הזאה as well. This completes the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know this also applies at קבלה, הולכה, and הזאה? The פסוק says "it shall be," meaning that during all its stages it must be תמים and בן שנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its teaching. This is the part that actually contradicts the answer in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "יהיה" is read as covering every stage of the עבודה, all the way to sprinkling the blood. If the animal must be תמים even at זריקה, then a loss after קבלה should disqualify it. That would undo the answer from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Carrying the blood to the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood
The פסוק teaches
Its stages of being, meaning all its עבודות

phrases.english: And from where do we know this applies at collection, conveying, and sprinkling?
The verse states: "shall be,"
that during all its stages it shall be
unblemished and in its first year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן בְּקַבָּלָה וְהוֹלָכָה וְהַזָּיָיה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 3, giving the challenge its force.
steps.raayaObject: That תמים is required even at זריקה, against step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of "יהיה" in Exodus 12:5.

steps.title: The ברייתא's later stages refer only to the age requirement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extension to קבלה, הולכה, and הזאה refers only to being בן שנה, not to being תמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explained the ברייתא as referring only to "in its first year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the later stages the animal must still be within its first year. But being תמים is required only up to קבלה. So a loss after קבלה remains acceptable, and step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He interpreted it (reading a source narrowly)
Short for על, "referring to"

phrases.english: He interpreted it as referring only to "in its first year,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both תמים and בן שנה are required through זריקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only בן שנה is required through זריקה. תמים is required only until קבלה.

steps.title: Support from רבי יהושע: blood is sprinkled even if only an olive-bulk remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading with רבי יהושע: for any קרבן, if even a כזית of meat or fat remains, the כהן still does זריקה. So the animal does not have to be whole at the time of זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, as it was taught: רבי יהושע says, for all the קרבנות in the תורה, if a כזית of meat or a כזית of fat remains, the כהן sprinkles the blood. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that its answer in step 5 is correct, and closes with "שמע מינה."
steps.deeperAnalysis: If almost the entire animal is gone and the blood is still sprinkled, then losing parts after קבלה clearly does not block זריקה. This shows that being whole is not required at זריקה. It confirms that the ברייתא's "יהיה" refers only to age.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces supporting proof)
תנא who rules on leftover portions of a קרבן
An olive-bulk, the minimum measure
The fats burned on the מזבח
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal must be תמים until קבלה. Being בן שנה is required through זריקה. A part lost after קבלה (like a kidney) does not disqualify the קרבן, as רבי יהושע shows: even a כזית remaining is enough for זריקה.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
from which there remains an olive-bulk of flesh
or an olive-bulk of fat:
he sprinkles the blood,
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings supporting proof for the answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the animal need not be תמים or whole at the time of זריקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ברייתא: blood is sprinkled if even a כזית of meat or fat remains.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A loss after קבלה does not disqualify the קרבן. The requirement at זריקה concerns only age (בן שנה).

steps.title: Can an animal turn two years old between slaughter and receiving the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that the animal must still be בן שנה at קבלה and הולכה. It seems impossible for the animal to age that fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing, where at the time of שחיטה the animal is in its first year, and at the time of קבלה and הולכה it is already in its second year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from Step 5. That answer said the extension to קבלה, הולכה and הזאה is about being בן שנה. The גמרא asks how that could ever matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלה and הולכה happen only moments after שחיטה. If age were counted in whole days or years, an animal could not change from 'one year old' to 'two years old' in those few moments. So why would the ברייתא need to teach this?

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really such a thing? (a challenge asking whether a case is even possible)
Carrying the blood to the מזבח
In its second year (too old for a פסח)

phrases.english: But is there anything
where at the time of slaughter it is in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִשְׁעַת קַבָּלָה וְהוֹלָכָה הָוֵי בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים?
phrases.english: and at the time of receiving and carrying the blood it is two years old?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from Step 5 that the ברייתא extends only the בן שנה requirement to the later stages.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the animal must still be בן שנה at קבלה and הולכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The time between שחיטה and קבלה is too short for an animal's age to change, so the teaching seems to have no real case.

steps.title: רבא: age of offerings is counted by the hour
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this ברייתא proves age in קדשים is counted by exact hours. So an animal really can pass its first birthday between שחיטה and קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that hours disqualify in קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The ברייתא itself shows that age is measured to the exact hour of birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal's year ends at that exact hour, it can turn two years old in the moments between שחיטה and קבלה. So the ברייתא is teaching something real. Such an animal becomes פסול for a קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches / this proves (learning a new rule from a source)
Hours disqualify, meaning age is counted by exact hours
Sacrificial animals

steps.whatToRemember: In קדשים, an animal's age is counted from the exact hour of its birth. That is why it can become too old in the middle of the עבודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: שעות פוסלות בקדשים is a well-known rule. It is learned from this ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This teaches
that hours disqualify with sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case is possible because age is counted by hours
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Age is counted roughly, so it cannot change in a few moments.
steps.terutzMaskana: Age is counted by exact hours, so the animal can become too old between שחיטה and קבלה.

steps.title: Proposal: the internal-lack question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main question about a missing internal organ. It suggests the question is a dispute between תנאים and starts quoting a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says the four blemishes in the פסוק are all in the ביצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a dispute of תנאים? The פסוק says 'bruised, crushed, torn, or cut.' All of these are in the ביצים. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier topic, whether a missing kidney (an internal lack) disqualifies a קרבן. It begins quoting a ברייתא to set up a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביצים are more hidden than the outer limbs. If רבי יהודה counts damage there as a blemish, he may hold that a hidden lack still counts as a lack. The full point will come in Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this matches a dispute of תנאים?
Bruised, crushed, torn, cut (the blemishes in ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ד)
The animal's testicles

phrases.english: Let us say it is a dispute of tanna'im:
"And bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut" —
all of them are in the testicles,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about age and returns to the main question of an internal lack, such as the kidney in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: all four blemishes in the פסוק apply to the ביצים.

steps.title: Only the testicles and not the penis?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יהודה. Does he really mean these blemishes count only in the ביצים and not in the גיד?
steps.simpleTranslation: Only in the ביצים and not in the גיד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא to question the words 'all of them are in the ביצים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גיד is more exposed and visible than the ביצים. It makes no sense that damage to the hidden part counts but damage to the visible part does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal's penis (outer organ)

phrases.english: In the testicles and not in the penis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי יהודה's statement in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'כולן בביצים,' which suggests only the ביצים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a hidden organ can be blemished, the more visible גיד surely can too.

steps.title: Correct the reading: also in the testicles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'also in the ביצים.' So רבי יהודה agrees the גיד counts and adds the ביצים as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: also in the ביצים. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read רבי יהודה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יהודה's view is that the blemishes count on the גיד and even on the hidden ביצים. His new point is that the hidden organ counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (correcting the reading of a text)
Also / even

phrases.english: Say: also in the testicles —
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה counts the blemishes only in the ביצים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה counts them in the גיד and also in the ביצים.

steps.title: The other opinions: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says all four blemishes count only on the גיד. רבי יוסי splits them: bruised and crushed count on the ביצים too, but torn and cut count only on the גיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: all of them are only on the גיד. רבי יוסי says: 'bruised and crushed' count also on the ביצים. 'Torn and cut' count on the גיד, yes, but on the ביצים, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. It now gives the two other opinions, which are needed for the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not count damage to the hidden ביצים at all. רבי יוסי takes a middle position, counting only some of the blemishes on the ביצים.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who holds the blemishes count only on the גיד
תנא who takes a middle position
Yes ... no

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
All of them are on the penis.
Rabbi Yosei says:
"Bruised or crushed" — also in the testicles;
"torn or cut" —
on the penis, yes; in the testicles, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא after the wording fix in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only on the גיד. רבי יוסי: bruised and crushed count also on the ביצים; torn and cut count only on the גיד.

steps.title: Is the dispute about whether a hidden lack counts as a lack?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנאים are arguing about our question. רבי יהודה holds a lack inside the body counts as a lack. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? One Sage holds a lack on the inside is called a lack. The other Sage holds it is not called a lack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the 'לימא כתנאי' suggestion. It links the blemish dispute to the earlier question about a missing kidney.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביצים are hidden, like an internal organ. רבי יהודה counts damage there, so a hidden lack counts. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not, so a hidden lack does not count. If this is right, our question about the kidney is simply a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that they argue about this? (proposing what a dispute is based on)
A lack on the inside of the body
One Sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion ('מאי לאו'). The גמרא rejects it in Step 14 and explains the dispute another way in Steps 15–17, so do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this:
that one Sage holds:
a lack on the inside is called a lack,
and the other Sage holds: it is not called a lack?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the full ברייתא from Steps 9 to 12 to finish the proposed link to the internal-lack question.
steps.raayaObject: That whether an internal lack counts as a lack is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יוסי about blemishes in the ביצים and גיד

steps.title: רבי יוסי's split position does not fit the suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the תנאים argue about an internal lack, because רבי יוסי's opinion would then contradict itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it this way? If so, what does רבי יוסי hold? If he holds that a lack inside the body counts as a lack, then even torn and cut ביצים should count. And if he holds that it does not count, then even bruised and crushed ביצים should not count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against its own suggestion from Step 13. That suggestion cannot explain רבי יוסי's middle opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument were only about whether a hidden, internal lack counts, every תנא would have to treat all four blemishes of the ביצים the same way. רבי יוסי counts bruised and crushed but not torn and cut. Under the Step 13 idea, that split has no basis, so the suggestion falls.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really understand it that way? A formula that rejects a suggestion.
A lack on the inside, meaning damage to a hidden or internal body part.
Torn: the ביצים are torn away from their attachment.
Cut: the ביצים are cut off from their attachment.

phrases.english: And can you really understand it this way?
What does Rabbi Yosei hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר חֶסְרוֹן מִבִּפְנִים שְׁמֵיהּ חֶסְרוֹן —
phrases.english: If he holds that a lack on the inside is called a lack,
phrases.notes: This would match רבי יהודה's view according to Step 13.

phrases.english: then even 'torn and cut' should also count!
And if he holds that it is not called a lack,
phrases.notes: This would match רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view according to Step 13.

phrases.english: then even 'bruised and crushed' should also not count!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in Step 13 that the ברייתא is a dispute about an internal lack.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the תנאים argue about whether an internal lack is a lack.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It cannot explain רבי יוסי, who treats the two pairs of blemishes differently. An all-or-nothing principle would force him to treat all four the same.

steps.title: New explanation: they argue about visible blemishes (רבי יהודה)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reading: the dispute is about blemishes that can be seen. רבי יהודה holds that all four are visible blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about blemishes that are visible. רבי יהודה holds: bruised and crushed is a מום, because the ביצים shrink. Torn and cut is a מום, because the ביצים hang down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to understand the whole argument. It starts with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is no longer about hidden damage at all. It is about whether each type of damage produces a change you can see. For רבי יהודה, bruised or crushed ביצים visibly shrink, and torn or cut ביצים visibly dangle, so all four count as a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes that are exposed or visible.
They are arguing.
Bruised or squeezed.
Crushed.
They shrink or shrivel.
They hang or dangle.

steps.confusionAlert: This explanation replaces the one in Step 13. Do not mix them: the question of an internal lack is no longer what the תנאים argue about.

phrases.english: Rather, here they argue about visible blemishes.
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
'bruised and crushed' is a blemish, because they shrink;
'torn and cut' is a blemish, because they hang down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from Step 13 with a new understanding of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the topic of the dispute: from internal lack to visible appearance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about whether a hidden, internal lack counts as a lack.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argue about whether each kind of damage creates a visible change. רבי יהודה says all four do.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: these changes look normal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that none of the four count on the ביצים, because healthy ביצים also sometimes shrink or hang.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds: bruised and crushed is not a מום, because even at the start, before any damage, the ביצים sometimes shrink. Torn and cut is not a מום, because even at the start they sometimes hang.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its new explanation and gives רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the question is about what you can see. But he says shrinking and hanging also happen to a healthy animal. Since the look is not unusual, it does not count as a visible מום.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, meaning before any damage happened.
Sometimes.
It is a blemish.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov holds:
'bruised and crushed' is not a blemish,
because even originally, they sometimes shrink;
'torn and cut' is not a blemish,
because even originally, they sometimes hang down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new explanation from Step 15 by giving the opposing view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the opposing תנא within the same new framework of visible blemishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב limits the four blemishes to the גיד, because on the ביצים these changes look like normal variation.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: crushed ביצים are gone, torn ones are still there
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts bruised and crushed as a מום because the ביצים are destroyed, but not torn and cut, because the ביצים are still present.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds: bruised and crushed is a מום, because the ביצים are no longer there in their normal form. Torn and cut is not a מום, because the ביצים are still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its new explanation by showing how רבי יוסי's middle position now makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the problem from Step 14. רבי יוסי's split is not about internal versus external. It is about whether the ביצים are still present: crushed ones are destroyed, while torn or cut ones are still in the pouch, even though they do not work.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not there; they no longer exist in their normal form.
They are there; they are still present.

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: all three תנאים argue about visible blemishes. רבי יהודה says shrinking and hanging both count. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says neither counts, since healthy animals look that way too. רבי יוסי says destroyed ביצים count, but ביצים that are still present do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step resolves the problem raised in Step 14. Every opinion in the ברייתא is now explained within one framework.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
'bruised and crushed' is a blemish, because they are no longer there;

phrases.aramaic: ״נָתוּק וְכָרוּת״ לָא הָוֵי מוּמָא — דְּהָא אִיתַנְהוּ.
phrases.english: 'torn and cut' is not a blemish, because they are still there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the new explanation and solves the difficulty about רבי יוסי raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives רבי יוסי a consistent reason that fits the new framework.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's split seemed to have no logic (Step 14).
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, it depends on whether the ביצים still exist: destroyed counts as a מום, still present does not.

steps.title: New משנה: damage to the pouch or to female genitalia
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins listing more blemishes: a damaged זובן, or damaged genitalia of a female sacrificial animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the זובן (the pouch covering the male organs) was damaged, or the genitalia of a female animal among קדשים was damaged, it is a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It continues the list of blemishes that make an animal unfit as a קרבן, which allows a בכור to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two items are a nick or loss of tissue in the male pouch, and the same kind of damage to a female's genitalia. The female case is mentioned in connection with מוקדשין, since a בכור is always male, but female sacrificial animals also become disqualified by blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה.
The pouch or sheath covering the male organs.
Genitalia.
Animals consecrated as קרבנות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the pouch was damaged,
or the genitalia of a female among consecrated animals,
phrases.notes: The word נפגם (was damaged) applies to this case too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the discussion of the ביצים ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage to the זובן, or to the genitalia of a female sacrificial animal, is a מום.

steps.title: משנה continues: blemishes of the tail
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists tail blemishes: a break in the bone (but not at a joint), a split tail tip with exposed bone, and a finger-width of flesh between vertebrae.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the tail was damaged at the bone, but not at the joint; or if the tip of the tail is split, meaning the skin and flesh were peeled off and the bone was left bare; or if there is a full finger-width of flesh between one vertebra and the next, these are all a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list, now with several kinds of damage to the tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damage to the bone of the tail is a מום, but damage at a joint is not, because a joint can heal. A split tail tip is explained as skin and flesh peeled away with bare bone showing. A gap of a full finger-width of flesh between vertebrae is also unusual enough to count.

keyTerms.meaning: Tail.
Joint, the connection between two vertebrae.
Split or peeled.
A vertebra or segment of the tail.
A full finger-width.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Split' here does not mean the bone is split in two. The משנה itself explains it: the skin and flesh were peeled off, leaving the bone bare.

phrases.english: If the tail was damaged at the bone,
but not at the joint,
phrases.notes: Damage at a joint heals, so it is not a מום.

phrases.english: or if the tip of the tail is split,
meaning the skin and flesh were peeled off and the bone remained,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּשָׂר מֵחוּלְיָא לְחוּלְיָא מְלֹא אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.english: or if there is flesh from one vertebra to the next a full finger-width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה's list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These tail injuries are a מום: damage to the bone (not the joint), a peeled tail tip with bare bone, and a full finger-width of flesh between vertebrae.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the sheath blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the זובן blemish applies only when the sheath is damaged, not removed. It also applies only to the sheath (כיס), not to the male organ itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אלעזר said: It is a blemish when the sheath was damaged, but not when it was removed. It is a blemish in the sheath, but not in the male organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the משנה's blemish of a damaged זובן (the sheath of the male organ). רבי אלעזר sets two limits on when it counts as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First limit: a nick or damage is a מום, but complete removal is not, apparently because a removed sheath can grow back. Second limit: the damage must be in the כיס (sheath), not in the זכרות (the organ itself).

keyTerms.meaning: was damaged or nicked
was removed entirely
the pouch or sheath (the זובן)
the male organ itself

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that damage is a blemish while full removal is not. The point is that a removed sheath can regrow (see Step 22), so removal is not a permanent מום.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Elazar said:
Damaged, but not removed;
phrases.notes: Only damage to the sheath is a blemish, not its full removal.

phrases.english: the pouch, but not the male organ.
phrases.notes: The blemish is in the sheath, not in the organ itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of Step 18 by defining the זובן blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זובן blemish applies to damage, not removal, and to the sheath, not the organ.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same two limits that רבי אלעזר stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא this way: damaged but not removed; the pouch but not the male organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says exactly what רבי אלעזר said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'תניא נמי הכי' brings support, not a challenge. רבי אלעזר's ruling now rests on an earlier tannaitic source, not only on his own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
damaged, but not removed;
the pouch, but not the male organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 20 with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's two limits on the זובן blemish

steps.title: A wolf-bitten sheath that grew back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם tells of an animal in עינבל whose sheath was taken by a wolf and later regrew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן המשולם said: There was an incident with an animal in עינבל whose sheath a wolf removed, and it returned to its full strength.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is brought that explains why full removal of the sheath is not a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The removed sheath grew back, so removal is not a permanent defect. This explains the 'ולא ניטל' half of רבי אלעזר's rule from Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident (a real case)
a wolf
returned to its original strength (it regrew)

steps.whatToRemember: The זובן blemish counts only when the sheath is damaged. If it is fully removed it can regrow, so it is not a lasting מום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam said:
There was an incident with one animal in Inbal
whose sheath a wolf removed,
and it returned to its strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם: מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the 'not removed' rule in Steps 20–21.
steps.raayaObject: That removal of the sheath is not a blemish
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case of a sheath that regrew after a wolf removed it

steps.title: Defining the finger measurement
steps.stepSummary: Turning to the tail blemish, a תנא defines the 'finger' mentioned in the משנה as one quarter of an average person's טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the tail was damaged from the bone, etc.' A תנא taught: The finger the Sages spoke of is one of four in a handbreadth of an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the tail blemish from Step 19, which spoke of a finger's width of flesh between vertebrae. It defines exactly how big that 'finger' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fingers differ in size, so the measure needs a fixed standard. It is set as one quarter of the טפח of an average person, not of a very large or very small one.

keyTerms.meaning: a finger-width measurement
a handbreadth (four finger-widths)
any ordinary, average person

phrases.english: 'If the tail was damaged from the bone, etc.'
A tanna taught:
The finger that they spoke of
is one of four in a handbreadth
of any average person.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְגְּמָה הַזָּנָב מִן הָעֶצֶם וְכוּ׳. תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the זובן discussion to the tail-blemish clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אצבע measure equals a quarter of an average person's טפח.

steps.title: Where else does this definition matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which area of הלכה this finger definition was taught for.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this taught?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. The גמרא wants to know which other law uses this definition of a finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrasing 'the finger that they spoke of' sounds like a general definition meant for other places in הלכה too. So the גמרא looks for the main law it was aimed at.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? (what practical difference does this make?)

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the application of the definition in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of הלכה the 'quarter-טפח finger' definition was taught for.

steps.title: רבה says it is for ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the definition applies to תכלת (ציצית). He opens a ברייתא where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue over how many strings to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is for the matter of תכלת, as it is taught: How many strings does one put in? בית שמאי say four, and בית הלל say three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his answer: the finger measurement matters for ציצית. He begins quoting a ברייתא as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part of the ברייתא is only about the number of strings. It sets the scene. The part that actually mentions the finger comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the blue thread of ציצית (here, ציצית in general)
strings
the school of שמאי
the school of הלל

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
for the matter of tekhelet (ritual fringes),
as it is taught in a baraita:
How many strings does one place?
Beit Shammai say: Four;
phrases.notes: Folded over, they make eight hanging strings.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Three.
phrases.notes: Folded over, they make six hanging strings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The finger definition applies to ציצית (תכלת).

steps.title: The hanging length uses this finger
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to the length of the hanging strings. בית הלל's three-finger length uses the quarter-טפח finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much should hang down? בית שמאי say four, and בית הלל say three. And the three that בית הלל speak of are each one of four in a handbreadth of an average person.
steps.whatsHappening: This part of רבה's ברייתא contains the actual proof. It uses the same 'quarter of a טפח' finger to measure the hanging strings of ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending of the ברייתא matches the תנא's definition in Step 23 word for word. So רבה concludes that the definition was taught for measuring ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: hanging down (the free length of the strings)
here: the three finger-widths that בית הלל require

phrases.english: And how much should be hanging?
Beit Shammai say: Four fingerbreadths;
and Beit Hillel say: Three.
And the three that Beit Hillel speak of
are each one of four in a handbreadth
of any average person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 25 and shows the matching wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the quarter-טפח finger definition is aimed at ציצית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's closing line, identical to the תנא's definition
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a sacrificial blemish measurement to the practical length of ציצית strings, showing that one standard finger-width is used across הלכה.

steps.title: רב הונא says it is for the two cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different answer. The definition relates to the two measuring cubits kept in the מקדש, as a משנה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: It is for the two cubits, as we learned in a משנה: There were two cubits...
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers another answer to 'for what law?' (Step 24). He points to the two measuring rods for cubits. The quoted משנה continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of ציצית, רב הונא connects the finger definition to the standard measuring rods in the מקדש. The details of how they fit come once the rest of the משנה is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: two cubits (two standard measuring rods)
as we learned in a משנה

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
for the two cubits,
as we learned in a mishna:
There were two cubits
phrases.notes: The משנה (כלים 17:9) continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: לִשְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to Step 24, parallel to רבה's answer in Steps 25–26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The finger definition relates to the two measuring cubits described in a משנה.
